title: Rescue work from a detached HEAD

scenario.brief:
You checked out an old commit to reproduce a bug — which put you in **detached HEAD**: HEAD points straight at a commit instead of at a branch. You then committed a fix right there. Git is now warning that your new commit isn't on any branch, and if you switch away it could be garbage-collected later.

The commit itself is fine; it just needs a branch to hold it. Your job: get that commit onto a branch so it's safe and can be opened as a pull request.

**Approach.** Create a branch at your current position — `git switch -c <name>` (or `git branch <name>`) — which both names this commit and attaches HEAD to the new branch. After that you're no longer detached, and the fix is preserved on a real branch.
scenario.whyItMatters: Detached HEAD is one of Git's most confusing states, and the warning text frightens people into losing work. Understanding that a commit only needs a branch to point at it — and how to attach one — turns a scary message into a two-second fix.

steps.message: fix: round tax to whole cents
steps.label: rescue

objectives.title: Get off the detached HEAD onto a branch
hints: `git status` says "HEAD detached at …". You need HEAD to point at a branch again.
`git switch -c <name>` creates a new branch at your current commit and moves you onto it.

objectives.title: Keep the fix commit — it must be on your branch
objectives.description: The rounding fix you committed while detached should now live on the branch you're on.
hints: Creating the branch at your current position captures the fix commit automatically.
If you switched to main first, you left the detached commit behind — go back with `git switch -` (or the reflog) and branch from there instead.
After `git switch -c <name>`, `git log --oneline` should show the rounding fix on top.

debrief.summary: You rescued a commit made on a detached HEAD by giving it a branch, so it's safe and shareable instead of dangling.
internals: Detached HEAD means HEAD holds a commit id directly rather than a `ref: refs/heads/...`. Commits you make still happen — HEAD just moves forward with no branch following.
Such commits are reachable only via HEAD and the reflog; switching away leaves them unreferenced, and `git gc` removes them eventually.
`git switch -c <name>` wrote a new branch ref at the current commit and pointed HEAD at that branch — so the commit is now reachable from a ref and safe.
You could equally have run `git branch <name>` to name the commit without moving, then switched to it.

keyCommands.note: Tells you when HEAD is detached, and at which commit.
Create a branch at HEAD and attach to it — the usual rescue.
Jump back to the previous location if you switched away by mistake.

commonMistakes: Switching to main while detached and assuming the commit is gone (it's still in the reflog).
Thinking detached HEAD is an error — it's a valid state, just not where you want to keep new work.
Branching after you've already moved away, so the branch starts from the wrong commit.
debrief.atWork: You land in detached HEAD whenever you check out a tag or an old commit to investigate. Knowing to branch before committing — or to branch immediately after — keeps investigative work from vanishing.
debrief.interview: "What is a detached HEAD and how do you save work from it?" Answer: HEAD points at a commit, not a branch; create a branch at that commit (git switch -c / git branch) so the work is referenced and safe.
